topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestReorgUnsafeHead`
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Filed by Claude on behalf of @ajsutton.

**CI run:** https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/123078/workflows/4327c7d8-ab80-44a4-9508-0c99d5bc2fe0/jobs/4868463/tests

**Job:** `memory-all-kona-op-reth` (acceptance tests)
**Date:** 2026-04-21
**Branch:** `gh-readonly-queue/develop/pr-20165-4df50ca0801bf0dd7049995d5a7c8cc8396023df` (merge queue)
**Test file:** `op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/reorgs/unsafe_head_test.go:113`

**Error:**
```
Error Trace: /home/circleci/project/op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/reorgs/unsafe_head_test.go:113
Error:       Should not be: 0xae78b3b90db8d7d10c044465707fc30e969695515bb3e778accb1554867a7831
Test:        TestReorgUnsafeHead
Messages:    Expected to get different heads on divergence block number, but got the same hash, so no reorg happened on chain A
```

Preceding log lines:

```
unsafe_head_test.go:111: Reorged chain A on divergence block number (prior the reorg) number=9 head=ae78b3..7a7831 parent=5aaa56..e2828e
unsafe_head_test.go:112: Reorged chain A on divergence block number (after the reorg) number=9 head=ae78b3..7a7831 parent=5aaa56..e2828e
```

**Context:**
- The test was unskipped and migrated to `TwoL2SupernodeInterop` in #20136 (commit `4df50ca080`).
- After `StopSequencer()`, the test uses `op-test-sequencer` to sequence a conflicting block at the unsafe head height, then calls `StartSequencer()` on the CL and waits for a new block.
- At the assertion, the block at the divergence height is still the original block — the EL's view of the unsafe head was never replaced by the test-sequencer's conflicting block (or the CL's resumed sequencing reverted the reorg).
- The test intersperses two `time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)` calls between `ia.New()` / `ia.Next()` at lines 97 and 101 — likely a timing race.

Will investigate and propose a fix.

topIssues.title: fix: cantina u19 #29 portal migration accepts bad targets
topIssues.author: stevennevins
topIssues.body:
migrateToSharedDisputeGame lets the ProxyAdmin owner replace both ethLockbox and anchorStateRegistry without validating the new contracts. The function only checks that Interop and ETHLockbox features are enabled, that the portal is not paused, that the caller is the ProxyAdmin owner and that the new registry differs from the old registry.

Consequently, a direct call can install a zero address, a non-contract address, a lockbox that has not authorized the portal or an AnchorStateRegistry that is not wired to the expected dispute-game factory and respected game type. This can brick deposits or withdrawals until another privileged operation repairs the portal configuration. It can also change the local pause identifier because SystemConfig.paused() uses the portal's lockbox address when the ETHLockbox feature is enabled.

The OPCM migrator performs important setup around this operation, including authorizing the portal on the new lockbox and migrating old lockbox liquidity. The portal does not enforce those assumptions itself, so the direct admin entrypoint remains easy to misuse.

topIssues.title: [PCD] Remove permissioned-only guard and dead anchor placeholder
topIssues.author: 0xOneTony
topIssues.body: `DeployOPChain.s.sol` today blocks any initial deployment whose `disputeGameType` is not `PERMISSIONED_CANNON` with a `require`, and hardcodes the `startingAnchorRoot` to `0xdead` through a helper. These two safeguards exist because the script was written when the genesis output root and the permissionless prestates were not available at deploy time. Now that both are computed earlier in the pipeline, remove the require, enable `CANNON` and `CANNON_KONA` with the prestate hashes coming in via the new input fields, and replace the placeholder anchor root with the computed value from the deploy input.

topPRs.title: feat: permissionless fault games at initial deploy
topPRs.author: lumoswiz
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Lets a new chain launch with permissionless fault games (Cannon and Cannon-Kona) enabled from genesis, not just the permissioned game. The deploy script used to require the permissioned game type and seed a placeholder anchor root. It now accepts the permissionless types, takes the real anchor root and per-game prestates as deploy inputs, and OP Contracts Manager allows those games at initial deploy. Default permissioned deploys are unchanged.

**Tests**
  * New chains using Cannon or Cannon-Kona now deploy, with both games enabled, the expected bonds and per-game prestates, and the anchor state registry seeded from the input.
  * Permissioned deploys still succeed and do not need the new permissionless inputs.
  * Invalid inputs revert: a missing or placeholder anchor root, missing prestates, and permissionless games requested alongside super roots.

**Additional context**

Part of the predictive-chain-deployments work (#20903). This PR adds and consumes the new deploy inputs, but they are still placeholders here. A follow-up (#20912) populates them from real pipeline state, so for now op-deployer and interopgen keep deploying the permissioned game with the old placeholder anchor and behavior does not change.

**Metadata**
  * Fixes #20913

topPRs.title: Feat/proof backfill batching
topPRs.author: dhyaniarun1993
topPRs.body:
**Description**

`op-proofs backfill` writes one MDBX transaction per block. On a 1.2 M-block extension that's 1.2 M commit/fsync round-trips. This PR batches K blocks into a single transaction.

- New flag: `--proofs-history.backfill-batch-size` (range 1..=100, default 50).
- Backfill on op-mainnet improvements: **8.3 → 22.5 blk/s (~2.7×)** on a 1.2 M-block run.
- See Caveats before assuming the same multiplier on your host.

**Failure semantics** 
A crash or validation error mid-batch drops the open RW transaction; up to K blocks of progress are lost. `earliest` in the proofs DB is unchanged, so the next run resumes from the same anchor and redoes them. Atomicity is preserved at batch granularity, not block granularity.

**Caveats**
- Hardware-sensitive - The 2.7× figure is from a 64 GB server. MDBX is memory-mapped and relies on the OS page cache for hot pages — at 64 GB, most of the trie working set stays resident, so the dominant per-block cost shifts to commit/fsync (which batching attacks directly). On a smaller host, per-block I/O would dominates instead, and the commit-reduction win shrinks.
- Cache-warmup ramp - When the proofs DB already has populated history tables (continuing a paused backfill, or re-running on an existing snapshot), the first several minutes run noticeably below the steady-state rate while the OS page cache reloads the hot trie/history pages. Throughput climbs as residency grows.

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: add post-fork L2 predeploy verification
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/202

Adds `just post-fork-ops` for verifying L2 predeploy contracts after a fork activation. Named `post-fork-ops` this way we can add more checks to it in the future, aside from just verifying contracts

L1 contracts are verified as part of their deployment. This command handles L2 predeploy proxies and implementations that are updated on existing chains as part of a fork.

Given an upgrade, the script:

1. Checks out the exact contracts source in a temporary worktree.
2. Reads the upgradeable predeploy list from that release's `Predeploys.sol`.
3. Fetches RPC and explorer metadata from the Superchain Registry.
4. Verifies each deployed predeploy proxy.
5. Reads each proxy's current implementation with `implementation()` and verifies that contract.
6. Reports what was already verified, newly verified, submitted, skipped, or failed.

The script automatically includes new upgradeable predeploys added to `Predeploys.sol`. Chains run concurrently with up to six workers, while logs and report data remain grouped and ordered by chain.

### Disabled implementations

An implementation is reported as disabled when the deployed proxy's `implementation()` call returns `address(0)`.

This means the predeploy proxy exists on the chain, but no implementation contract has been configured for it. There is therefore no implementation address or bytecode to verify. The script still verifies the proxy and reports its implementation as skipped instead of treating the intentionally empty implementation as a failure.

For U19 on the tested chains, this applies to:

- `CrossL2Inbox`
- `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger`
- `SuperchainETHBridge`
- `ETHLiquidity`
- `NativeAssetLiquidity`
- `LiquidityController`

For U19, the script maps to `op-contracts/v7.0.0-rc.3` and source commit `79a83f3ce70b0f3c54cb058a1140fa50e57268bc`, where the Karst NUT bundle was generated.

## Testing

- `bash -n packages/contracts-bedrock/scripts/post-fork-ops/verify-predeploys.sh`
- `shellcheck packages/contracts-bedrock/scripts/post-fork-ops/verify-predeploys.sh`
- `just -f packages/contracts-bedrock/justfile post-fork-ops --help`
- Six-chain mainnet dry run for OP, Ink, Unichain, Mode, Metal, and Zora: 40 applicable targets and six disabled implementations per chain, zero failures.
- Dry run through the renamed `post-fork-ops` entrypoint for OP and Ink: 40 applicable targets and six disabled implementations per chain, zero failures.
- Live concurrent OP and Ink verification: 40 already-verified targets and six disabled implementations per chain, zero failures.
- Invalid chain slug: exited nonzero and reported the failed chain worker.
